body.statement: For all \(G\equiv_E H\) and \(e\in E(H)\setminus E(G)\), \(G+e\equiv_E G\) for every \(e\in U_{\to}\cup U_{\leftrightarrow}\). This includes SCC-changing arrows, directed self-loops, unordered bidirected loops \(\{u,u\}\), arbitrary directed cycles, and bidirected additions outside occupied SCC rectangles.
body.justification: This local theorem resolves the global conjecture by iteration.
body.gap: No published E-result covers these unrestricted regimes.
body.consumer: Equivalent representatives become connected by safe edge additions.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove that every profile-changing edge occurring in an E-equivalent comparison graph is individually safe to add to the base graph.
obligation.obstruction: The fixed-profile splice only replaces edges already represented by directed paths or by an occupied cross-SCC bidirected rectangle in the base lift.  Equality of E-models supplies only past-to-future separation queries with the target-dependent conditioning set \(D(B,C)\); it has not been shown to determine the endpoint marks, copy indices, ancestry certificates, and SCC-tail certificates needed to splice an arbitrary profile-changing edge.  The published greatest-element theorem for homogeneous weak \(\mu\)-equivalence cannot be imported: E-equivalence restricts both endpoint layers and conditioning sets in a target-dependent, non-homogeneous way, and E-separation is not \(\mu\)-separation on the original DMG.
obligation.attempted: The fixed-profile replacement, antitonicity, first-new-edge minimality, singleton composition, a potential-parent/potential-sibling reduction patterned on \(\mu\)-separation, and a two-copy-lift reduction to homogeneous weak equivalence were checked.  The latter two routes require marked connectivity information not encoded by any declared frozen node.  Independently, the prescribed exhaustive gate tested every one of the \(384168\) loop-free five-vertex bases with at most five edges.  It performed \(12105891\) signature comparisons, covering \(708990\) individually safe additions and \(129303\) same-signature collisions, and found no failure.  Exhaustive loop-inclusive checks through three vertices also found no failure, but neither finite calculation proves the universal claim.
obligation.partial_result:
For every \(e\in E(\Gamma(G))\setminus E(G)\), the fixed-profile theorem gives \(G\equiv_E\Gamma(G)\), while
\[
 G\subseteq G+e\subseteq\Gamma(G).
\]
The interval part of antitonicity therefore proves \(G+e\equiv_EG\).  This covers exactly the directed completions internal to a non-singleton SCC, the completions of an already occupied incoming-to-SCC support, and the bidirected completions of an already occupied cross-SCC rectangle, with both loop conventions retained by \(\Gamma\).  It does not prove safety for an edge that changes this profile.  The independent finite falsification gate over the loop-free five-vertex universe checked all \(384168\) bases having at most five edges, all \(400\) nontrivial singleton queries per signature, \(708990\) individually safe additions, and \(129303\) same-signature collisions; no unsafe admissible union or collision union was found.  This finite computation is evidence only and supplies no universal implication.
